item.title: Stop Polling for Releases, Let Them Push to Your CI: Angelia, a Self-Hosted Release Event Bus
item.description: GitHub Actions cannot react to a release of someone else’s repository, so plugin maintainers poll on a cron that GitHub says can be late or dropped. Angelia watches PyPI, npm, crates.io, GitHub and GitLab for you and pushes one signed event per new version. Home Assistant 2026.11.2 was detected 3 seconds after it was published and tested in my integration’s CI an hour later. And 10,000 watches fit in 1 vCPU and 256 MB.

item.title: New Week, Another AI Coach: ai-finance-coach
item.description: A self-hosted coach for your household’s money. PSD2 bank sync through Enable Banking, an encrypted local database, a one-time login link or a passkey, and a language model that only ever receives redacted, pseudonymised, already computed figures. With real examples of what stays on your machine and what is sent.

item.title: Searching Proton Photos like it's Google Photos: how I built proton-faces
item.description: E2E encryption means Proton can never index your photos. So I built a two-container search engine that does it locally, on my own hardware, without ever writing back to Proton.
